about.title: Burbank Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: There is no right way to grieve, and there is certainly no convenient moment to think about paperwork. Still, when a death in Burbank was caused by someone else's carelessness—on the Golden State Freeway, along Glenoaks Boulevard, at a job site, or in a care facility—California law gives certain family members the right to bring a civil claim. That claim is separate from any criminal case the district attorney may or may not pursue. Under state law, a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children have first standing; certain dependents and heirs may follow. Compensation can cover funeral and burial expenses, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the harder-to-measure loss of their love, companionship and guidance. The deadline is generally two years from the date of death, and shorter if a public agency is involved. LawProactive is not a law firm. We connect Burbank families with an independent attorney who handles wrongful death cases on contingency, so there is nothing to pay unless there is a recovery.

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California limits who may bring a wrongful death claim, starting with a spouse or domestic partner and children, then certain dependents and heirs. The attorney we connect you with can sort out standing for your family before anything else.

items.title: Two-year deadline, watched closely
items.desc: The general filing window is two years from the date of death, and it shrinks considerably when a city, county, or state agency may share fault. Getting connected early protects your options.

items.title: The full picture of loss
items.desc: Recoverable damages go beyond funeral and burial costs to include lost financial support and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance. A civil claim also proceeds on its own track, regardless of whether criminal charges are filed.

items.question: Burbank reported zero traffic deaths in 2025. Does that mean wrongful death claims are rare here?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Burbank did record 209 injury collisions and 297 people injured in 2025, and wrongful death claims arise from far more than traffic, including workplace incidents, medical negligence, unsafe property, and defective products. Every family's situation is different, and an attorney can tell you whether the facts of your loss support a claim.

items.question: My family member died in a crash on the I-5 or SR-134 in Burbank. Is the deadline different?
items.answer: It may be. If a public entity such as Caltrans or the City of Burbank could be partly responsible—for example, because of roadway design or maintenance—California requires a government claim to be filed within a much shorter window than the standard two years. That is one reason we encourage families to get connected with an attorney sooner rather than later.

items.question: The person responsible is facing criminal charges. Do we have to wait for that case to end?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action that is separate from any criminal prosecution in Los Angeles County, and it can move forward on its own timeline. A conviction is not required, and an acquittal does not automatically end the civil claim. The attorney you are connected with can explain how the two cases may interact.
